Vue.js

Complete Reference & Concept Guide v3.5.x Node.js 18+ Released May 2026

Vue is a progressive JavaScript framework for building user interfaces. This guide covers all core concepts, Composition API, reactivity, and practical code examples for Vue 3.5.

Installation

# Create a new Vue application with Vite (recommended)
npm create vue@latest myapp

# Interactive prompts: TypeScript, JSX, Router, Pinia, etc.

# Or create manually with Vite
npm create vite@latest myapp -- --template vue
# With TypeScript
npm create vite@latest myapp -- --template vue-ts

# Install dependencies
cd myapp
npm install

# Start development server
npm run dev

# Build for production
npm run build

# Preview production build
npm run preview

Single-File Components (SFC)

Vue SFCs use the .vue extension with three sections: template, script, and style.

Basic SFC Structure
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'

const count = ref(0)
</script>

<template>
  <div class="counter">
    <h1>Hello Vue!</h1>
    <p>Count: {{ count }}</p>
    <button @click="count++">Increment</button>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.counter { text-align: center; }
h1 { color: #42b883; }
</style>
SFC Features
<!-- <script setup> -- shorthand Composition API -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue'
defineProps<{ title: string }>()
const emit = defineEmits<{ update: [value: string] }>()
</script>

<!-- Scoped CSS -- isolated styles -->
<style scoped>
.parent > .child { font-weight: bold; }
/* Deep selector for child components */
:deep(.child-component) { color: red; }
/* Slotted content */
:slotted(span) { text-decoration: underline; }
/* Global selector within scoped */
:global(.global-class) { font-size: 2rem; }
</style>

<!-- Multiple style blocks -->
<style module>
.blue { color: blue; }  /* $style.blue in template */
</style>

Template Syntax

<!-- Text interpolation -->
<p>{{ message }}</p>

<!-- Raw HTML (use cautiously) -->
<div v-html="rawHtml"></div>

<!-- Attribute bindings -->
<img :src="imageUrl" :alt="altText" />
<div :id="dynamicId" :class="{ active: isActive }"></div>

<!-- Dynamic attribute names -->
<button :[attributeName]="value">Dynamic</button>

<!-- Class & Style bindings -->
<div :class="['static', { active: isActive }, dynamicClass]"></div>
<div :style="{ color: textColor, fontSize: size + 'px' }"></div>

<!-- Event handlers -->
<button @click="handleClick">Click</button>
<button @click="count++">Inline</button>
<input @keyup.enter="submit" />

<!-- Event modifiers -->
<form @submit.prevent="onSubmit">...</form>
<a @click.stop="doThis" href="#">Stop</a>
<div @click.once="fireOnce">Once</div>

<!-- Mouse / keyboard modifiers -->
<input @keydown.ctrl.enter="save" />
<div @mousemove.self="move">Self only</div>

<!-- Conditional rendering -->
<div v-if="visible">Visible</div>
<div v-else-if="otherCondition">Other</div>
<div v-else>Hidden</div>
<template v-if="loading"><Spinner /></template>

<!-- v-show (toggles display: none) -->
<div v-show="visible">Shown/Hidden</div>

<!-- List rendering -->
<ul>
  <li v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">
    {{ item.text }}
  </li>
</ul>

<!-- With index -->
<li v-for="(item, index) in items" :key="index">{{ index }}: {{ item }}</li>

<!-- Over object -->
<li v-for="(value, key) in object" :key="key">{{ key }}: {{ value }}</li>

Reactivity

Vue 3's reactivity system is based on ref and reactive with automatic dependency tracking.

ref & reactive

import { ref, reactive, computed, watch, watchEffect } from 'vue'

// ref â€” wraps primitive values (and objects)

const count = ref(0)
count.value = 5  // access via .value

console.log(count.value)

// reactive â€” wraps objects only

const state = reactive({
  name: 'Vue',
  version: 3.5,
})
state.name = 'Vue.js'  // direct property access


// ref with objects (automatically becomes .value)

const user = ref({ name: 'Alice', age: 30 })
user.value.age = 31

// Template auto-unwraps refs

// <p>{{ count }}</p>  â€” no .value needed in template


// computed

const double = computed(() => count.value * 2)

// writable computed

const fullName = computed({
  get: () => `${firstName.value} ${lastName.value}`,
  set: (val) => {
    const parts = val.split(' ')
    firstName.value = parts[0]
    lastName.value = parts[1]
  },
})

Watch

import { watch, watchEffect } from 'vue'

// Watch a single source

watch(count, (newVal, oldVal) => {
  console.log(`count changed from ${oldVal} to ${newVal}`)
})

// Watch multiple sources

watch([firstName, lastName], ([newFirst, newLast], [oldFirst, oldLast]) => {
  console.log('Name changed')
})

// Watch with deep option

watch(user, (newVal) => {
  console.log('User deeply changed', newVal)
}, { deep: true, immediate: true })

// flush: 'post' â€” run after DOM update

watch(count, callback, { flush: 'post' })

// watchEffect â€” auto-tracks dependencies

watchEffect(() => {
  console.log(`Count is: ${count.value}`)
  // auto-tracks any reactive refs used inside

})

// Async watcher â€” oneShot

watch(source, (newVal, oldVal, onCleanup) => {
  const controller = new AbortController()
  onCleanup(() => controller.abort())
  fetch(`/api?q=${newVal}`, { signal: controller.signal })
})

toRef & toRefs

import { toRefs, toRef, reactive } from 'vue'

const state = reactive({ x: 0, y: 0 })

// Convert all properties to refs

const { x, y } = toRefs(state)

// Convert a single property to a ref

const xRef = toRef(state, 'x')

// Keeps reactivity linked to original state

x.value = 10  // also updates state.x

Composition API

The Composition API organizes component logic by feature rather than option. <script setup> is the recommended syntax.

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, computed, onMounted } from 'vue'
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router'

// Props (no need to import defineProps)

const props = defineProps<{
  title: string
  initialCount?: number
}>()

// Emits

const emit = defineEmits<{
  update: [value: number]
  delete: [id: string]
}>()

// Expose

defineExpose({ reset })

// Reactive state

const count = ref(props.initialCount ?? 0)
const double = computed(() => count.value * 2)

// Methods

function increment() {
  count.value++
  emit('update', count.value)
}

// Lifecycle

onMounted(() => {
  console.log('Mounted!')
})

// Router

const router = useRouter()
function navigate() {
  router.push('/dashboard')
}
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <h1>{{ title }}</h1>
    <p>Count: {{ count }} (double: {{ double }})</p>
    <button @click="increment">+1</button>
  </div>
</template>
Options API (Legacy - still supported)
export default {
  props: ['title'],
  emits: ['update'],
  data() {
    return { count: 0 }
  },
  computed: {
    double() { return this.count * 2 }
  },
  methods: {
    increment() { this.count++; this.$emit('update', this.count) }
  },
  mounted() { console.log('Mounted!') }
}

Components

Props & Emits
<!-- Child Component -->
<script setup lang="ts">
// Type-based props

defineProps<{
  title: string
  items: string[]
  count?: number          // optional

  status: 'active' | 'inactive'
}>()

// With defaults

interface Props { title?: string; count?: number }
const props = withDefaults(defineProps<Props>(), {
  title: 'Default Title',
  count: 0,
})

// Emits

const emit = defineEmits<{
  (e: 'update', id: number): void
  (e: 'delete', id: number): void
}>()

// Or simpler syntax

const emit = defineEmits<{
  update: [id: number]
  delete: [id: number]
}>()

emit('update', 42)
</script>

Slots

<!-- Child Component (BaseLayout.vue) -->
<div class="layout">
  <header>
    <slot name="header">Default header</slot>
  </header>
  <main>
    <slot />  <!-- default slot -->
  </main>
  <footer>
    <slot name="footer" />
  </footer>
</div>

<!-- Parent usage -->
<BaseLayout>
  <template #header>
    <h1>Custom Header</h1>
  </template>

  <p>Default slot content</p>

  <template #footer="{ year }">
    <footer>© {{ year }}</footer>
  </template>
</BaseLayout>

<!-- Scoped slots -- passing data back to parent -->
<!-- Child -->
<slot name="item" :item="item" :index="index" />

<!-- Parent -->
<template #item="{ item, index }">
  <li>{{ index }}: {{ item.name }}</li>
</template>

Provide / Inject

import { provide, inject, type InjectionKey } from 'vue'

// Define injection key

const USER_KEY = Symbol('user') as InjectionKey<User>

// Provider (ancestor)

provide('theme', 'dark')
provide(USER_KEY, { name: 'Alice', role: 'admin' })

// Injector (descendant)

const theme = inject('theme', 'light')  // with default

const user = inject(USER_KEY)           // typed


// Reactive provide

const count = ref(0)
provide('count', readonly(count))  // prevent mutation

count.value++                       // child still reacts

Vue Router

// router/index.ts

import { createRouter, createWebHistory } from 'vue-router'

const router = createRouter({
  history: createWebHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/', name: 'home', component: () => import('@/views/Home.vue') },
    { path: '/about', name: 'about', component: () => import('@/views/About.vue') },
    {
      path: '/users',
      children: [
        { path: '', name: 'users', component: () => import('@/views/UserList.vue') },
        { path: ':id', name: 'user', component: () => import('@/views/UserProfile.vue'), props: true },
      ],
    },
    { path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*', name: 'not-found', component: () => import('@/views/NotFound.vue') },
  ],
  scrollBehavior(to, from, savedPosition) {
    if (savedPosition) return savedPosition
    return { top: 0 }
  },
})

// Navigation guard

router.beforeEach(async (to, from) => {
  const auth = useAuthStore()
  if (to.meta.requiresAuth && !auth.isAuthenticated) {
    return { name: 'login', query: { redirect: to.fullPath } }
  }
})

export default router

Pinia

Pinia is the official state management library for Vue 3, with TypeScript support and devtools integration.

// stores/counter.ts

import { defineStore } from 'pinia'
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'

export const useCounterStore = defineStore('counter', () => {
  // State

  const count = ref(0)
  const name = ref('Counter')

  // Getters

  const double = computed(() => count.value * 2)

  // Actions

  function increment() { count.value++ }
  async function fetchAndSet() {
    const data = await fetch('/api/count')
    count.value = await data.json()
  }

  return { count, name, double, increment, fetchAndSet }
})

// Component usage

import { useCounterStore } from '@/stores/counter'

const store = useCounterStore()
store.count       // reactive state

store.double      // computed getter

store.increment() // action


// Destructure with reactivity

const { count, double } = storeToRefs(store)
const { increment } = store // destructure action directly

Composables

Composables are functions that use Vue's Composition API to encapsulate reusable logic.

// composables/useFetch.ts

import { ref, onUnmounted } from 'vue'

export function useFetch<T>(url: string) {
  const data = ref<T | null>(null)
  const error = ref<string | null>(null)
  const loading = ref(true)
  const controller = new AbortController()

  async function execute() {
    loading.value = true
    error.value = null
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal })
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch')
      data.value = await res.json()
    } catch (err: any) {
      if (err.name !== 'AbortError') error.value = err.message
    } finally {
      loading.value = true && false  // force

      loading.value = false
    }
  }

  onUnmounted(() => controller.abort())

  execute()

  return { data, error, loading, refresh: execute }
}

// composables/useMouse.ts

import { ref, onMounted, onUnmounted } from 'vue'

export function useMouse() {
  const x = ref(0)
  const y = ref(0)

  function update(e: MouseEvent) {
    x.value = e.pageX
    y.value = e.pageY
  }

  onMounted(() => window.addEventListener('mousemove', update))
  onUnmounted(() => window.removeEventListener('mousemove', update))

  return { x, y }
}

// Usage in component

const { data: todos, loading, error } = useFetch<Todo[]>('/api/todos')
const { x, y } = useMouse()

Transitions & Animations

<!-- Single element/component -->
<Transition name="fade" mode="out-in">
  <p v-if="visible">Hello</p>
</Transition>

<!-- List transitions -->
<TransitionGroup name="list" tag="ul">
  <li v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">{{ item.text }}</li>
</TransitionGroup>

<!-- CSS classes generated by transition name -->
.fade-enter-active, .fade-leave-active {
  transition: opacity 0.3s ease;
}
.fade-enter-from, .fade-leave-to {
  opacity: 0;
}

/* List move animation */
.list-enter-active, .list-leave-active {
  transition: all 0.4s ease;
}
.list-enter-from, .list-leave-to {
  opacity: 0;
  transform: translateX(30px);
}
.list-move {
  transition: transform 0.4s ease;
}

<!-- JavaScript hooks -->
<Transition
  @before-enter="onBeforeEnter"
  @enter="onEnter"
  @after-enter="onAfterEnter"
  @leave="onLeave"
>
  <div v-if="show"></div>
</Transition>

Forms

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue'

const form = reactive({
  name: '',
  email: '',
  password: '',
  category: 'general',
  agree: false,
})

const errors = ref<Record<string, string>>({})

function validate(): boolean {
  const errs: Record<string, string> = {}
  if (!form.name.trim()) errs.name = 'Name is required'
  if (!form.email.includes('@')) errs.email = 'Invalid email'
  if (form.password.length < 6) errs.password = 'Min 6 characters'
  errors.value = errs
  return Object.keys(errs).length === 0
}

function handleSubmit() {
  if (!validate()) return
  console.log('Submit:', form)
  // API call...

}

// VeeValidate integration (popular)

import { useForm, useField } from 'vee-validate'
import { toTypedSchema } from '@vee-validate/zod'
import { z } from 'zod'

const schema = toTypedSchema(z.object({
  name: z.string().min(2),
  email: z.string().email(),
}))

const { handleSubmit: vHandleSubmit } = useForm({
  validationSchema: schema,
})

const { value: name, errorMessage: nameError } = useField('name')
const { value: email, errorMessage: emailError } = useField('email')
</script>

<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
    <input v-model="form.name" placeholder="Name" />
    <span v-if="errors.name">{{ errors.name }}</span>

    <input v-model="form.email" type="email" placeholder="Email" />
    <span v-if="errors.email">{{ errors.email }}</span>

    <select v-model="form.category">
      <option value="general">General</option>
      <option value="support">Support</option>
    </select>

    <label>
      <input v-model="form.agree" type="checkbox" /> I agree
    </label>

    <button type="submit">Submit</button>
  </form>
</template>

Testing

// Component test with Vitest + Vue Test Utils

import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'
import Counter from './Counter.vue'

describe('Counter.vue', () => {
  it('renders initial count', () => {
    const wrapper = mount(Counter, { props: { initialCount: 5 } })
    expect(wrapper.text()).toContain('5')
  })

  it('increments on button click', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(Counter)
    await wrapper.find('button').trigger('click')
    expect(wrapper.text()).toContain('1')
  })

  it('emits update event', async () => {
    const wrapper = mount(Counter)
    await wrapper.find('button').trigger('click')
    expect(wrapper.emitted('update')).toBeTruthy()
    expect(wrapper.emitted('update')![0]).toEqual([1])
  })
})

// Composition API test

import { ref, computed } from 'vue'

function useCounter(initial = 0) {
  const count = ref(initial)
  const double = computed(() => count.value * 2)
  const increment = () => count.value++
  return { count, double, increment }
}

describe('useCounter', () => {
  it('starts at initial value', () => {
    const { count } = useCounter(10)
    expect(count.value).toBe(10)
  })

  it('increments correctly', () => {
    const { count, increment } = useCounter()
    increment()
    expect(count.value).toBe(1)
  })
})

Best Practices

Component Design — Use <script setup> by default. Keep components small and focused. Extract reusable logic into composables.
Project Structure
src/
  components/    # Reusable components
    BaseButton.vue
    BaseCard.vue
  composables/   # Reusable logic
    useFetch.ts
    useAuth.ts
  views/         # Page-level components
    Home.vue
    UserProfile.vue
  router/
    index.ts
  stores/        # Pinia stores
    counter.ts
    user.ts
  utils/         # Helpers
    format.ts
  types/         # TypeScript types
    index.ts
  App.vue
  main.ts
Key Guidelines
  • Use Composition API + <script setup>
  • Use TypeScript for type safety
  • Extract composables for reusable logic
  • Use Pinia for global state
  • Always use :key in v-for
  • Use scoped styles by default
  • Lazy-load routes with dynamic imports
  • Use v-model on custom components
  • Handle loading and error states
  • Test with Vitest + Vue Test Utils
